## About me

::: {.hv-lead}
I am a geomicrobiologist from Croatia, doing my PhD in the
[Geomicrobiology Group](https://uni-tuebingen.de/fakultaeten/mathematisch-naturwissenschaftliche-fakultaet/fachbereiche/geowissenschaften/arbeitsgruppen/geo-und-umweltnaturwissenschaften/geo-und-umweltnaturwissenschaften/geomikrobiologie/arbeitsgruppe/people/)
at the University of Tübingen, as part of a DFG Emmy Noether project.
:::

Bacteria have lived on Earth for more than three billion years, but they rarely leave
clear fossils. I grow mats of sulfur- and iron-cycling bacteria, then "cook" them under
hot, high-pressure conditions like those deep in the Earth's crust, to see which of their
shapes and chemical traces survive. Knowing what a fossilized microbe looks like helps us
read the oldest rocks on Earth, and tells rover missions what to look for on Mars.

My path here went from environmental sciences in Zagreb (my bachelor thesis already
asked whether Mars was once habitable), through North Pacific plankton, sea-turtle
microbiomes and zebrafish ecotoxicology, to experimental fossilization.
